newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down sharply at an intraday low of 8.2930 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Thursday, from a two-year high of 8.2900 on Wednesday, mainly due to profit-taking, traders said.
Some spectulative selling in the last few minutes of trading also helped depress the local currency, they said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2910.

The yuan opened lower at an intraday high of 8.2905 and fell slightly to move around 8.2910 for most of the session before it slipped further late in trading. Trading was more active than Wednesday with most business done at 8.2912, traders said.
Traders said heavy profit-taking emerged at the opening on Thursday after the yuan hit its two-year high on Wednesday.
"The yuan faced heavy selling pressure at the 8.2900 level, which forced it to reteat," one trader said.
A second trader said buyers seemed to have no intention to push the yuan through the key 8.2900 resistance level, leading to some speculative selling in the last few minutes of trading.
Traders said the yuan was likely to rebound on Friday.
The yuan ended up at 7.2343 from 7.2412 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0700 from 1.0690 vs the Hong Kong dollar.
